best_moment.what: Telling them exactly why it would fail in The Counter. I only learned from the ending card that it removed my ceiling, so it was a good surprise in hindsight, though I didn't feel it at the time.

worst_moment.what: The Committee of Supply, where I rebranded a scheme with a higher number. It was a dull dilemma with jargon I didn't follow, and it just cost me some INTEG.

answer.held_back_by: The file capped me at Deputy Secretary from the start, and my honesty cost me standing along the way. I never got to politics, and the card suggests the Counter choice took me outside the service's normal path. I still don't fully understand why I was stuck.
answer.ending_fair_why: I reached the top grade, kept my integrity high and earned a lot, and the declassified card explained things clearly. I would have liked to see the Tea payoff and the Leak reveal. Neither seemed to land, which was a bit frustrating.
answer.chase_next: The politics route. I never found out what the Tea led to, and I want to see whether being invited into politics is a different ending from retiring as Perm Sec.
answer.play_again_why: The ceiling reveal made me curious how different choices change the path, and I want to try for politics. But the middle years were slow, so I would be hoping for more happening.
answer.title_fit_why: The game is about being tested, confirmed in grades and having your standing and integrity matter. Pay is shown every year, but my run was about the career and not the money.
